notes: "The two friends were big now." — 'big' for 'grown up' is acceptable at A1, but "The two friends were grown up now." is more natural and matches the other levels.
"His tears washed the splinter out." — the reader has met two pieces (eye and heart); "His tears washed the splinter out of his eye." would be clearer.
The word Kai must spell is never named at A1 ("made the word"); acceptable, since 'the word' points back to 'He wanted to make a word with them.'

issues.quote: He broke the roses and laughed at Gerda's tears.
issues.problem: 'Broke the roses' is an odd collocation; a native children's author would not say you 'break' roses. Other levels correctly use 'pulled up' / 'tore'.
issues.fix: He pulled up the roses and laughed at Gerda's tears.

notes: "Kai began to cry too, and his tears washed the splinter out." — two splinters were introduced; consider "washed the splinter out of his eye" for clarity.
'forever' (A2/B1) vs 'Eternity' (B2/C1) is an acceptable simplification of the original word.
"The crow told her about a clever young man who married the princess of that land." — 'who had married' is more precise, but past simple is acceptable at B1.
The reindeer saying "She was going to Lapland" is consistent with the original, where the reindeer knows the Snow Queen's summer tent is in Lapland.
"She put on her new red shoes and offered them to the river, and a drifting boat carried her away." — skips Gerda climbing into the boat; acceptable condensing.

"scribbled a few words on a dried cod and sent them on to a wiser woman in Finland" — 'them' could grammatically refer to 'a few words' instead of Gerda and the reindeer; "and sent the travellers on" removes the ambiguity.

"though the whole world and the new skates no longer interested him in the least" is an interpretive addition not stated by Andersen; it doesn't contradict the original, and quiz Q3 is supported by the text as written, so not a failure.

summary: Faithful to Andersen at every level: mirror, splinters, sleigh, the garden with painted roses, crows, prince and princess, robber girl, Lapp and Finn women, snowflake army, Mirror of Reason, Eternity, the tears and the grown-up return. Level control and quizzes are sound. The one concrete defect is the unnatural collocation 'He broke the roses' at A2; with the one-line fix it should pass.
